Package com.nis1.thesis.sdk

Interface CoreSystemApi

public interface CoreSystemApi
API exposed by the Core System to all embedded (in-process) pluggable modules.

This interface provides both publishing and subscription capabilities for the event-driven architecture. It is implemented by the Module Registry's SdkModuleHost, which holds embedded modules and dispatches events to them in-memory, and which forwards a subset of published events onward to RabbitMQ.

There is no AMQP topic exchange or routing-key matching anywhere in this path: publishing and subscription are both implemented as plain in-memory dispatch keyed by the event's type string, and the one RabbitMQ hop involved uses a single named, durable queue via the default exchange (channel.basicPublish("", queueName, ...)). Standalone (non-embedded) modules communicate purely over RabbitMQ named queues and never go through this interface at all.

  • Method Details

    • publishEvent

      void publishEvent(Event<?> event)
      Publishes an event from an embedded module.

      The current implementation only forwards events whose type starts with the literal prefix "alerts."; events with any other type are accepted but silently dropped (not forwarded, not queued, not dispatched to subscribers). Forwarded events are serialized to JSON and published with basicPublish("", udmIngressQueue, ...) to a single fixed named queue on RabbitMQ's default exchange — there is no exchange, routing key, or per-type queue involved.

      Parameters:
      event - The event to publish, containing type and payload data. Must not be null.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if event is null
      RuntimeException - if publishing fails due to network or broker issues

    • subscribeToEvent

      void subscribeToEvent(String eventType, Consumer<Event<?>> listener)
      Subscribes an embedded module to events of a specific type or prefix.

      This is in-memory dispatch, not AMQP topic routing. Registered listeners are matched against dispatched events in two ways only:

      • Exact match — eventType equals the event's type exactly.
      • Single-level prefix wildcard — an eventType ending in ".*" (e.g. "odl.*") matches any event type starting with that prefix (e.g. "odl.host.isolate").

      Full AMQP topic algebra (multi-segment # wildcards, * matching a single arbitrary segment anywhere in the pattern) is not supported.

      Parameters:
      eventType - The exact event type, or a "prefix.*" pattern, to subscribe to. Must not be null or empty.
      listener - The callback function to handle received events. Must not be null.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if eventType is null/empty or listener is null
      RuntimeException - if subscription fails due to network or broker issues
